The first public release of **up**, a self-hosted HTTP uptime monitor with a terminal UI.

A single Go binary with embedded SQLite. No database server, no agents, no YAML.

## Highlights

- **HTTP checks:** URL, interval, timeout and expected status per monitor, with the failure reason when one goes down.
- **Create monitors in the TUI:** add them from a form; the running daemon picks them up within seconds, without a restart.
- **Catch up on what you missed:** every result is stored, so you see recent checks and outages when you SSH back in.
- **Stale-daemon detection:** if the daemon stops writing, the TUI says so instead of marking your services down.
- **Retention:** results older than 30 days are removed automatically (`--retention` to change it).
- **One-line install:** a script that verifies the checksum and can set up the systemd service.

## Getting started

Binaries are available for **Linux/amd64** and **Linux/arm64**:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giulianotesta7/up/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --service
```

Drop `--service` to install only the binary. Then run `up tui` and press `n` to add your first monitor.

[Documentation](https://github.com/giulianotesta7/up/blob/v0.1.0/README.md)
